ablations.prompt: Can you please explain what inflation is? My cousin is 10. Use simple words Thanks so much!

runs.answer:
Sure! Inflation is when things get more expensive over time.

Imagine a candy bar that cost 50 cents when your parents were kids. Today, that same candy bar might cost $1.50. The candy bar didn't get better. It just costs more money now. That's inflation.

When inflation happens, each dollar can buy a little less than it could before. So if you have $5 saved up, it might buy fewer toys next year than it does today.

Most of the time, prices go up slowly, a little bit each year. Grown-ups and governments keep an eye on it to make sure prices don't go up too fast.

Inflation is when things slowly cost more money over time.

Imagine a candy bar that costs $1 today. If prices go up with inflation, next year that same candy bar might cost $1.05. Your money buys a little less candy than it did before, even though you still have the same amount of money.

Why does it happen? Usually because lots of people want to buy things, but there isn't quite enough stuff to go around, so stores can charge more. Sometimes making things gets more expensive too, like when ingredients or gas cost more, and stores pass that cost along to shoppers.

Grown-ups watch inflation closely, because if prices go up too fast, it gets hard for families to afford things they need.
